justifications.functional_suitability: The Real-Time Scoring Engine addresses R-01, while Case Management & Analytics API, PostgreSQL, and Frontend Web App cover R-02. However, while Rule & Model Configurator exists, there is no direct path or mechanism to hot-reload rules into the scoring engine without downtime (R-03).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS is supported by Go on ECS Fargate, HTTP/2 ingress, and in-memory feature caching via Amazon ElastiCache (Redis). Asynchronous offloading uses AWS Kinesis Data Streams, although direct S3 writes from the Audit Logger Component could threaten latency budgets if synchronous.
justifications.compatibility: Integrates with external Merchant / Payment Gateway systems using standard HTTP/2 and gRPC/TLS protocols via ALB Ingress Router. Redis RESP protocol, PostgreSQL TCP/SQL, and standard REST/OIDC protocols are cleanly utilized across internal and external boundaries.
justifications.usability: Fraud Analysts are well-served via Frontend Web App components including Case Management Dashboard and Rule & Model Configurator. Authentication & Session Manager integrates smoothly with AWS Cognito to govern operational access.
justifications.reliability: The Fallback Circuit Breaker Component in the Real-Time Scoring Engine ensures payments are not blocked if scoring dependencies fail (R-07). Amazon ElastiCache multi-AZ replication provides caching resiliency, though cross-AZ or gateway-level failover mechanics for total engine outages lack full definition.
justifications.security: PCI-DSS and 7-year tamper-evident auditability are enforced via Amazon S3 with Object Lock, AWS KMS, AWS WAF, and Cognito. Data Masking Middleware in REST/GraphQL Handler prevents analysts from viewing full PANs, though a dedicated tokenization service is not explicitly detailed.
justifications.maintainability: Managed AWS services (RDS, ElastiCache, Fargate) drastically reduce operational burden for a 3-engineer team. Clear modular separation exists between scoring and case management, though treating CloudFront and Cognito as child components inside Frontend Web App in C4 is structurally anomalous.
justifications.portability: Architecture aligns with the target AWS eu-west-1 region, but heavy architectural coupling to proprietary AWS primitives (Kinesis, S3 Object Lock, KMS, Cognito, WAF) significantly impedes portability to alternative cloud providers or on-premises environments.

PERF-01.justification: The Go-based scoring engine using HTTP/2, local in-memory evaluation, and Redis O(1) feature lookups directly supports sub-50ms latency. However, direct synchronous writes from the Audit Logger to S3 risk introducing tail-latency spikes under 3,000 req/s if not strictly routed via Kinesis.
sensitivity_points: Network latency and serialization overhead between the scoring engine and ElastiCache Redis.
Ensuring audit logging operations remain fully asynchronous off the hot decision path.
tradeoffs: Using asynchronous buffering prevents latency spikes but risks transient in-flight log drops during crashes.

PERF-02.justification: Analyst workloads are physically decoupled from the scoring path. The Case Management API connects to Amazon RDS PostgreSQL using a dedicated read replica for analytics queries, completely isolating database load and CPU utilization from the Real-Time Scoring Engine and Redis.
sensitivity_points: Separation of read replica traffic from transactional primary database connections.
Resource isolation between case management APIs and the real-time scoring cluster.
tradeoffs: Replication lag from RDS read replicas can display slightly stale analytical metrics to analysts.

AVAIL-01.justification: While an in-memory Fallback Circuit Breaker exists inside the Scoring Evaluator, it cannot handle total container crashes or host outages. The ALB lacks defined failover targets or automated static fallback routes when the backend scoring service is completely unavailable.
sensitivity_points: Health check interval and failover routing configuration at the ALB ingress layer.
Ability to execute fallback logic outside the crashing application runtime.
tradeoffs: Local circuit breaking adds minimal latency but fails completely during total process termination.

AVAIL-02.justification: The Audit Logger streams events asynchronously via AWS Kinesis Data Streams and SQS queues, decoupling scoring execution from audit store degradation. Even if S3 Object Lock writes slow down, queuing absorbs backpressure without degrading P99 decision latency.
elements: AWS Kinesis Data Streams / Amazon SQS
Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS
sensitivity_points: Buffer retention limits and backpressure handling in Kinesis Data Streams during S3 outages.
Non-blocking client configuration within the Go Audit Logger Component.
tradeoffs: Decoupled message streaming requires additional operational monitoring to manage consumer lag.

MOD-01.justification: ECS Fargate supports zero-downtime rolling updates and fast container rollbacks. However, the architecture defines no dynamic model registry, runtime model loader, or traffic splitting mechanism, requiring full container redeployments to update models rather than zero-downtime hot-reloading.
sensitivity_points: Container image deployment speed and container startup initialization time on AWS Fargate.
Inclusion of model version metadata in generated decision output payloads.
tradeoffs: Immutable container updates enhance reproducibility but slow down emergency rollbacks compared to dynamic toggles.

MOD-02.justification: The Rule & Model Configurator exists in the frontend, but there is no architectural link or message channel connecting it or the Case Management API to the Real-Time Scoring Engine to propagate rule updates at runtime without rebuilding and restarting containers.
sensitivity_points: Absence of a control plane or pub/sub mechanism to sync rules to scoring engines.
Rule engine evaluation capabilities inside the Go scoring evaluator component.
tradeoffs: Compiling rules into engine code ensures execution speed but prevents rapid runtime updates.

SEC-01.justification: The REST/GraphQL Handler includes data masking middleware and Cognito enforces RBAC to prevent analysts from viewing clear-text card data. However, the architecture provides no SIEM, CloudWatch alarm, or anomaly detection mechanism to detect compromised accounts within 15 minutes.
sensitivity_points: Strict enforcement of data masking middleware across all API serialization pathways.
Lack of behavioral analytics or automated alerting for anomalous analyst token usage.
tradeoffs: Server-side data masking protects PAN data but increases API CPU processing overhead.

SEC-02.justification: The system implements Amazon S3 with Object Lock (WORM storage) and pg_partman partition archiving, backed by AWS KMS keys. Decision inputs, model versions, and explainability records are immutably preserved for 7 years and queryable within one working day.
elements: Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS
sensitivity_points: S3 Object Lock retention policy configuration and bucket compliance modes.
Indexing scheme for retrieving historical partitions from S3 cold storage.
tradeoffs: Offloading aged partitions to S3 minimizes RDS hosting costs but lengthens historical lookup time.
